quote: Our life is an apprenticeship to the truth, that around every circle another can be drawn; that there is no end in nature, but every end is a beginning; that there is always another dawn risen on mid-noon, and under every deep a lower deep opens.
source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Circles, Essays, Essay X, the opening paragraph, p. 249 (James Munroe, 1841)
note: The locator was corrected. In the 1841 James Munroe edition this sentence closes the opening paragraph of Essay X on page 249; it is not the second paragraph. Later editions print a verse motto above the essay, and the 1841 page has none. The wording, with its comma after truth, is the 1841 text.
